title: On the Basics of Ideal Moscow Spaces
content: The purpose of this paper is to introduce and investigate a basic ideal-theoretic extension of the notion of a Moscow space. A classical Moscow space is a topological space in which the closure of every open set can be represented as a union of Gδ-subsets of the ambient space. We introduce the notion of an I-Gδ set by requiring a set to differ from a Gδ set by an element of a prescribed ideal I. This leads to the definition of an ideal Moscow space. We establish elementary relationships between Moscow spaces and ideal Moscow spaces, including monotonicity with respect to the ideal, invariance under homeomorphisms, and sufficient conditions based on countable pseudocharacter. Examples illustrate the definition and its dependence on the ideal. We also discuss heredity, products, and mappings, distinguishing proved statements from questions that require additional hypotheses. The proposed framework provides a starting point for a systematic study of Moscow-type properties in ideal topological spaces.
